risks.title: PACE_SOURCE_IN ESTIMATED path is registry-valid but never emitted
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.2.5 — Pace Source Evidence/Risk Alignment (deferral originally made and documented in Phase 4D.2 — PACE_SOURCE_IN Resolver Implementation)
risks.statement: The runtime condition registry defines PACE_SOURCE_IN.ESTIMATED as a valid value, but Backend Integration Phase 4D.2's PaceSourceResolver deliberately never emits it: no approved estimation methodology was found anywhere in the repository for deriving a pace source from runningBackground / recentWeeklyVolumeKm / recentLongestRunKm / recentRunsPerWeek alone. As a result, a user who supplies training-volume evidence but no recent race result and no target finish time currently resolves to NONE, not ESTIMATED. This is acceptable while the resolver remains unwired from live generation, but it is activation-relevant: before PACE_SOURCE_IN output is ever consumed by real plan generation, product must decide how this user population should be classified.
requiredResolution: Approve and document a V1 estimation methodology for ESTIMATED (e.g. from training-volume evidence), and implement it in PaceSourceResolver; or
Explicitly decide V1 will not use ESTIMATED at all and update registry/docs accordingly (e.g. mark it reserved-for-future-version); or
Keep ESTIMATED reserved but explicitly confirm product/UX accepts NONE as the outcome for training-volume-only users.
Do not implement an unapproved estimation method to close this risk.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume PACE_SOURCE_IN (not specific to any catalog candidate version)
risks.implementationNote: Backend Integration Phase 4D.5.1 (cross-risk finding, discovered during Phase 4D.5 orchestration testing): if the ESTIMATED path described above is later implemented, OR PaceSourceResolver's output priority (currently RECENT_RACE > TARGET_TIME > NONE) changes for any other reason, re-verify GoalFeasibilityResolver behavior for the combination PACE_SOURCE_IN=NONE with targetFinishTimeSeconds present. Reason: as of Phase 4D.5, GoalFeasibilityResolver's own PACE_SOURCE_NONE_TARGET_TIME_REQUESTED branch is unreachable through real RuntimeConditionResolutionService.ResolveAll orchestration, because PaceSourceResolver already emits TARGET_TIME (not NONE) whenever targetFinishTimeSeconds exists -- GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN never sees PACE_SOURCE_IN=NONE while a target time is also present under the current pipeline. This is a behavioral dependency between the two resolvers' logic, not a type-system guarantee -- nothing prevents a future change to PaceSourceResolver's priority order (e.g. if ESTIMATED is introduced ahead of TARGET_TIME, or the priority order is otherwise revised) from making this branch reachable again with different semantics than originally intended. See PHASE4D_5_RUNTIME_CONDITION_RESOLVER_ORCHESTRATION_SERVICE.md ('a new finding') and PHASE4D_5_1_PACESOURCE_GOALFEASIBILITY_CROSS_RISK_NOTE.md for full detail. This note does not change PaceSourceResolver or GoalFeasibilityResolver behavior -- it only records the dependency for future re-verification.

risks.title: AsOfDate preview/confirm lifecycle semantics not wired
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.2.5 — Pace Source Evidence/Risk Alignment (field originally added in Phase 4D.2 — PACE_SOURCE_IN Resolver Implementation)
risks.statement: PaceSourceResolver computes recent-race-evidence age (and the associated recency-confidence metadata) relative to RuntimeResolverContext.AsOfDate, an explicit evaluation-date field added in Phase 4D.2 specifically so the resolver never reads the wall clock directly. However, the live preview/confirm request lifecycle does not yet supply or persist an AsOfDate anywhere -- no code populates this field outside of tests. Before any future phase wires PaceSourceResolver into live generation, product/engineering must decide: does AsOfDate get fixed at preview-generation time and then reused unchanged at confirm (for preview/confirm consistency), or does it get recomputed fresh at confirm time (allowing recency to reflect any delay between preview and confirm)? No repository evidence resolves this question either way.
requiredResolution: Decide whether confirm reuses the preview's AsOfDate or recomputes it independently.
Wire whichever behavior is chosen into the live preview/confirm flow when PaceSourceResolver is eventually connected to generation.
Do not silently default to wall-clock time at confirm without an explicit product decision.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume PACE_SOURCE_IN recency metadata (not specific to any catalog candidate version)
risks.implementationNote: Backend Integration Phase 4E.1.1 (governance clarification pass): Phase 4E.1 computed AsOfDate exactly once per preview (DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.UtcNow), never re-read per resolver) and threaded it unchanged through the pilot resolver pipeline and into the frozen CatalogPreviewSnapshot.AsOfDate field -- see PHASE4E_1_CATALOG_PREVIEW_ROUTING_AND_IMMUTABLE_RESOLUTION_SNAPSHOT.md section 7. This satisfies the preview-side half of PaceSourceResolver's own AsOfDate contract, but does NOT touch this TD's actual closure criteria, all three of which are about CONFIRM: whether confirm reuses the preview's AsOfDate unchanged or recomputes it independently, and wiring that decision in. Phase 4E.1 does not wire catalog generation into confirm at all (by design), so none of the three requiredResolution items are satisfied yet. Intended closure path: Phase 4E.2, which must read the frozen AsOfDate from the stored CatalogPreviewSnapshot at confirm time and make (and wire) an explicit reuse-vs-recompute decision -- never silently default to wall-clock time at confirm. This TD may legitimately remain OPEN even after Phase 4E.2 ships if that phase implements snapshot-reuse mechanically without an explicit, recorded product decision on which policy (reuse vs. recompute) is correct. Backend Integration Phase 4E.2 acceptance-finalization pass addendum (appended, not replacing the above; status NOT changed to closed -- reconciled per PHASE4E_2_CLAUDE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md section 17 and PHASE4E_2_FINAL_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md): CatalogPlanConfirmationService.BuildPlan now explicitly reads StartedAt from snapshot.AsOfDate and never recomputes it from DateTime.UtcNow (ConfirmedAtUtc is kept strictly separate, technical-only). RESOLVED by this: (a) preview freezes AsOfDate exactly once; (b) confirm code, where wired, does not recompute AsOfDate; (c) confirm does not rerun resolver orchestration to derive AsOfDate or anything else; (d) an immutable preview/confirm snapshot-consistency boundary now exists in code. UNRESOLVED, and NOT covered by this TD's own tracked closure criteria: persistable stage-to-week schedule generation (GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload is still always null -- BuildPlan's AsOfDate-reuse code is not reachable in production because the step-11 persistability guard rejects every real snapshot first, so the reuse decision has never been exercised against real traffic); calendar-day alignment (does not exist); production concurrent-confirmation safety (no DB-level preview-to-plan uniqueness invariant exists -- tracked as a Blocking Defect in PHASE4E_2_CLAUDE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md section 15, not part of this TD's own scope); and public catalog activation (still blocked by the PUBLISHED-only eligibility gate, independently of this TD). This TD is NOT closed: its own three requiredResolution items are substantively addressed by (a)-(d) above, but the repository's established convention (see TD-CORE-READINESS-001's own precedent) is not to mechanically close a risk whose implementation has not yet been exercised against real, live traffic -- the AsOfDate-reuse code path in BuildPlan has never actually run against a real confirm request. Re-review for closure once a future phase makes GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload reachable and this code path is genuinely exercised.

risks.title: CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN thresholds are not approved
risks.statement: CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN registry values exist (READY / CAUTION / NOT_READY). Phase 4B provides optional evidence fields (recentWeeklyVolumeKm, recentLongestRunKm, recentRunsPerWeek) that could in principle feed a readiness classification. No approved threshold mapping was found anywhere in the repository to convert those fields into READY / CAUTION / NOT_READY: the only evidenced threshold set (golden-fixture-v3's CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_RESOLVER, rule TEN_K_STANDARD_ENTRY: minimumWeeklyVolumeKm=20, minimumLongestRunKm=8, minimumRunsPerWeek=3) is a single pass/fail gate with no failing example and no CAUTION/NOT_READY boundary evidenced at all, its output ("STANDARD") is not even a valid registry value for this condition type (see TD-REGISTRY-001), and Phase 4A.2 already classified this exact threshold set's scope as 'D — not approved / DECISION_REQUIRED'. Backend Integration Phase 4D.3 therefore implemented CoreEntryReadinessResolver as an always-NotEvaluated placeholder — it never emitted READY, CAUTION, NOT_READY, or STANDARD under any input.
requiredResolution: Approve V1 READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY readiness thresholds, with an explicit, evidenced boundary for all three values (not just a single pass gate); or
Explicitly decide CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN will remain NotEvaluated/unused in V1; or
Update registry/docs accordingly if the intended shape differs from a three-tier classification.
Do not implement guessed thresholds to close this risk.
risks.resolutionNote: Backend Integration Phase 4D.3.1: product owner explicitly approved V1 READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY thresholds as an internal canonical decision (recorded as EV-008 in evidence-log.json; full mapping in PHASE4D_3_1_CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_THRESHOLD_DECISION_AND_RESOLVER_ACTIVATION.md). CoreEntryReadinessResolver now implements real classification logic (READY: weekly>=15 AND longest>=6; NOT_READY: weekly<8 OR longest<4; CAUTION: otherwise, including partial-evidence cases; both-missing: NOT_READY only in a GoalType=Race context, else NotEvaluated). recentRunsPerWeek remains metadata-only per the same owner decision, never a hard gate. STANDARD is still never emitted -- confirmed by test. This risk is NOT mechanically closed (consistent with this file's existing convention of never closing a risk outright, e.g. TD-WAVE5-001's own 'revisited, not closed' precedent) because a residual risk remains: the resolver is still not wired into live generation, and its output has not yet been exercised against real, live user traffic. Re-review before any future wiring of this resolver into generation.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN (not specific to any catalog candidate version)

risks.title: Tier-1 Golden Fixture references EASY_SHAKEOUT, but no validated, versioned EASY_SHAKEOUT workout definition exists in the resolved v10 catalog bundle
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4F.6 Pre-Implementation Step C (V1 Pilot Workout Progression, Fixed Role Binding, and Governance Decisions); originally proposed during Step B (phase4f6-step-b-training-science-evidence-mapping.json, easyShakeoutRiskRecommendation) following the user's own preceding proposal
risks.statement: The tier-1 canonical Golden Fixture v3 references a workout key, EASY_SHAKEOUT, that does not exist as a validated, versioned workout definition anywhere in the resolved v10 catalog bundle (catalog/workouts/ contains no easy-shakeout.*.json). EASY_WITH_STRIDES (named only in architecture-spec example vocabulary and other governance prose) shares the same divergence pattern. The V1 pilot's fixed EASY_SUPPORT binding (D-C07: EASY_SUPPORT -> EASY_STANDARD) deliberately does not add either key.
risks.severity: See blocking scope below (non-uniform across steps)
requiredResolution: Add a validated, versioned EASY_SHAKEOUT (and/or EASY_WITH_STRIDES) workout definition and an explicit binding/policy referencing it; or
Revise Golden Fixture v3 to use only accepted catalog keys; or
Explicitly reclassify the fixture field as illustrative/non-canonical.
Do not add EASY_SHAKEOUT or EASY_WITH_STRIDES to the catalog to close this risk without an explicit product/schema decision (D-C12 remains DEFERRED).
risks.currentRuntimeImpact: None — workout binding is not yet implemented (Phase 4F.6B is not started) and the fixture is not consumed as a production workout-definition source.
risks.closureNote: Phase 4F.6B (V1 Exact Workout Definition Binding): closed via the third requiredResolution option — 'explicitly reclassify the fixture field as illustrative/non-canonical' — not via renaming the fixture (first option) or adding EASY_SHAKEOUT to the catalog (explicitly prohibited). Direct inspection of the fixture's EASY_SHAKEOUT occurrence (docs/canonical/golden-fixture-v3/golden-10k-intermediate-4d-12w.v3.plandocument.json, W12_D3) shows fields with no equivalent in EASY_STANDARD's schema at all: raceEveShakeout=true and raceEveDistanceCapKm=4 — a specialized, race-eve-specific shakeout-run semantic (a capped, short distance the day before a race), not a stylistic variant of a generic easy run. Renaming this occurrence to EASY_STANDARD (the first requiredResolution option) would therefore be factually incorrect, not merely conservative — it would erase real, distinct semantic content the fixture actually encodes. This mirrors the repository's own already-accepted precedent for the exact analogous case: domain-wave1-schema-necessity-audit.md's finding that the fixture's LONG_RUN_PROGRESSION key 'is a distinct, non-substitutable workout key, not evidence for LONG_RUN_STANDARD itself.' Applying the same reasoning here: EASY_SHAKEOUT is formally reclassified as an illustrative reference to a distinct, richer, not-yet-built V1 workout concept (a specialized race-eve taper session) — never evidence that V1's EASY_SUPPORT binding should resolve to anything other than the accepted EASY_STANDARD fixed default (D-C07). The fixture itself was NOT modified — it remains an accurate historical/reference artifact; only its governance interpretation for V1 binding purposes is now formally recorded. EASY_WITH_STRIDES (architecture-spec example vocabulary only, never present in the fixture itself) is unaffected by this closure and remains a separate, still-open vocabulary question if/when it is ever proposed as a real catalog artifact.
risks.closureCriteriaSatisfied: Third requiredResolution option ('explicitly reclassify the fixture field as illustrative/non-canonical') fully satisfied for EASY_SHAKEOUT specifically. First and second options not pursued (renaming would be factually incorrect; adding the workout definition remains explicitly deferred, D-C12).

risks.title: GoalFeasibilityResolver PACE_SOURCE_IN=TARGET_TIME branch could not distinguish a product-average planning reference from an unverified user-typed performance claim
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.4.1 (Product-Average Target-Time GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN Classification), triggered by acceptance test SW-02
risks.statement: Every target finish time reaching GoalFeasibilityResolver via PACE_SOURCE_IN=TARGET_TIME collapsed into one NotEvaluated/PACE_SOURCE_TARGET_TIME_NO_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE outcome (HTTP 422 via NotEvaluatedReasonClassifier/ApplyNotEvaluatedGovernancePolicy), with no contract-level way to distinguish the Flutter client's own canonical 'go with average' planning reference from an unverified user-typed capability claim. SW-02 (a fully valid 10K/Intermediate/4-day/12-week product-average request) was rejected as a direct consequence.
requiredResolution: Add an explicit, required target_finish_time_source field to the Race request contract distinguishing product_average from user_defined; or
Otherwise formally approve treating every target time identically regardless of provenance (rejected as unsafe -- would either weaken user-defined safety or keep product-average blocked).
risks.currentRuntimeImpact: None remaining -- product_average requests now receive an explicit Evaluated/CHALLENGING classification; user_defined requests are completely unaffected.
risks.closureNote: Phase 4D.4.1: target_finish_time_source (product_average/user_defined) added to ResolverInputSnapshot and threaded from the new GenerateRacePlanPreviewRequest public contract. GoalFeasibilityResolver's TARGET_TIME branch now returns Evaluated/CHALLENGING/PACE_SOURCE_TARGET_TIME_PRODUCT_AVERAGE_ACCEPTED for product_average (value validated against CanonicalTargetFinishTimePolicy at the request-validation boundary, HTTP 400 on mismatch, before this resolver ever runs). user_defined (and any legacy/unset caller) keeps the exact prior NotEvaluated/PACE_SOURCE_TARGET_TIME_NO_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE behavior, unchanged. No registry value, golden fixture, or candidate status was modified.
risks.closureCriteriaSatisfied: First requiredResolution option fully satisfied: target_finish_time_source is now an explicit, required, validated field on the Race contract, and GoalFeasibilityResolver branches on it deterministically.

risks.title: Foundation Compression Readiness Gate Is Undefined
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3A — Eight-Week Race-Core Allocation Audit (governance follow-up)
risks.source: PHASE4G_3A_EIGHT_WEEK_CORE_ALLOCATION_AUDIT.md section 5a (Clarification -- N=8 mootness does not resolve the general C-03 question); backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Resolvers/CoreEntryReadinessResolver.cs; backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/Materialization/CatalogPhaseAllocation.cs; plan-catalog/catalog/templates/ten-k-master.v6.json
risks.statement: For the current exact-8-week TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE core (the only 8-week allocation the catalog's own minimums permit: F2/B3/RS2/T1), Foundation does not compress to 1 week -- the active catalog minimum for FOUNDATION is 2, so this question is not applicable to today's pilot. This does NOT resolve the general product/runtime rule for future horizons or candidates where Foundation=1 may become structurally possible (e.g. a shorter horizon, a revised candidate, or a future catalog minimum change): no confirmed repository artifact currently defines which CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN outcomes (READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY) would permit Foundation=1 if and when it becomes structurally reachable. Future horizon-aware compression work must not enable Foundation=1 without an explicit readiness-gating decision. The runtime already resolves CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN for every catalog-routed request today (CoreEntryReadinessResolver is registered in production DI and invoked by RuntimeConditionResolutionService.ResolveAllResults) and its result is already in scope at the phase-allocation call site -- so the open issue is decision/contract ownership (which readiness outcomes permit Foundation=1, and which layer decides), not absence of the signal itself.
affectedAreas: Any future sub-12-week race-core implementation phase (e.g. Phase 4G.3B and beyond)
requiredResolution: Before any future allocation permits Foundation=1, explicitly define whether CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN=READY permits Foundation=1.
Explicitly define whether CAUTION permits Foundation=1, forbids it, or requires a different (non-Foundation=1) allocation instead.
Explicitly define whether NOT_READY always forbids Foundation=1.
Identify which layer owns this eligibility decision (e.g. the phase-allocation resolver itself, an upstream routing/service-layer guard, or a dedicated policy).
Define how the phase allocator consumes CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN's already-computed result without re-running or duplicating resolver evaluation.
Define the typed, fail-closed result that applies when a target horizon structurally requires Foundation=1 but the runner's CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN outcome is not eligible.

Do not enable Foundation=1 for any allocation without this decision being explicitly recorded first -- do not silently infer it from the N=8 finding, which does not apply (N8_STATUS: NOT_APPLICABLE_DUE_TO_CATALOG_MINIMUM_2).
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE version or descendant candidate whose future horizon-aware core allocation would require FOUNDATION below its currently-active catalog minimum of 2 weeks -- not applicable to any currently-supported horizon, including the current exact-12-week pilot and the current exact-8-week audit finding (F2/B3/RS2/T1)

risks.title: NotEvaluated Resolver Results Silently Route to Fallback Stages Without Confirmed Product Approval
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3B StageReachabilityVerifier work, validation and follow-up pass (2026-07-23)
risks.statement: ProgressionStageAllocator.IsStageEligible computes `satisfied = result.Status == RuntimeConditionResolutionStatus.Evaluated && result.OutputValue is not null && condition.AllowedValues.Contains(result.OutputValue)`, and returns false whenever this is not true. This means a runtime condition resolver returning NotEvaluated (the resolver could not decide) and a resolver returning Evaluated with an output value outside the stage's AllowedValues (the resolver decided the condition is not met) are treated identically: both make `satisfied=false`, and ResolveEligibility then walks the stage's FallbackStageKey exactly the same way for either case. No runtime code currently distinguishes 'the resolver couldn't decide' from 'the resolver decided the condition isn't met' when routing a conditional progression stage to its fallback. This was discovered during Phase 4G.3B's StageReachabilityVerifier work, which deliberately delegates all stage-selection logic to the real ProgressionStageAllocator (proving the verifier introduces no second scheduling algorithm) and in doing so surfaced this pre-existing behavior. This is structurally the same category of gap as AUD-008 / TD-ALLOCATION-PRIORITY-001: an existing runtime behavior with no traceable product/coaching approval, discovered by a verification pass rather than authored as a deliberate decision.
affectedAreas: Every conditional progression stage with a FallbackStageKey (e.g. GOAL_PACE_REHEARSAL -> CURRENT_FITNESS_SPECIFIC_REHEARSAL)
StageReachabilityVerifier (Phase 4G.3B.3b, mechanical-only, not yet publicly wired)
Any future safety-verification or support-registry work that depends on distinguishing resolver indecision from resolver rejection
requiredResolution: A product decision is required on whether NotEvaluated should continue to silently fall back to the alternate stage (current behavior), or whether it should instead block/flag the affected week for a different treatment (e.g. surfacing a DecisionRequired-style outcome instead of silently substituting).

This decision must be made, or this risk must remain OPEN and be explicitly factored into any future safety-verification or support-registry work, before NotEvaluated-triggered fallback routing is treated as verified-safe production behavior.
Do not fix or change the NotEvaluated-to-fallback behavior itself without this decision being explicitly recorded first.
